finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF and local file read: the POST parameter 'feed' is passed directly to file_get_contents(), which accepts http(s)://, ftp://, file://, php:// and other wrappers. The response length is echoed, so it works as an oracle for internal services and files. The attacker can probe cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) and internal hosts, and can learn whether a URL or file exists and how large it is.

trace.note: Entry condition: POST request with 'feed' set. Only checks the request method and isset, with no authentication.
The user-controlled value is passed unmodified to file_get_contents(), which makes the outbound request or reads the local file.
strlen of the fetched body is echoed back to the attacker, giving a blind-SSRF oracle.

finding.guards_checked: No scheme or host allowlist, no private/link-local IP blocking, no DNS-resolution check, and no require_admin() call. The require_admin() function is defined at line 4 but is not called on this path. Session start does not gate it.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes $_POST['feed'] unvalidated to file_get_contents() and echoes strlen of the result, with no auth check (require_admin() at line 4 is only called at line 18 on a different path) and no scheme or host allowlist.

finding.claim: SSRF through the webhook setter: the 'set_webhook' POST parameter is passed to curl_init() and the request is executed with curl_exec(), with no URL validation. cURL follows the supplied scheme, so gopher://, file://, dict:// and internal http targets are possible. The path is restricted to admin sessions, which lowers severity, but there is still no restriction on internal destinations, and any admin-session compromise or a CSRF against an admin could reach it.

trace.note: $hook is assigned from the user-controlled value.
curl_exec() sends the request to the attacker-chosen destination.

finding.guards_checked: Only require_admin() (admin session check, lines 4-9). No scheme/host allowlist, no private/link-local IP filtering, no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction, and no CSRF token. The response is not returned to the caller, so this is blind SSRF.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() session check only (import.php:4-9, 18); no URL/scheme/host validation
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (import.php:17-22), but the sink is reachable only after require_admin() at import.php:18 passes, so $_POST['set_webhook'] is an admin-only input and not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker (the CSRF angle is speculative, and the separate unauthenticated 'feed' SSRF at line 12 is a different finding).
